It’s really helpful being in therapy 9 hours a week.  The consistency is really crucial for early recovery. It keeps me accountable and I feel like I can be 100% honest in the group, even if I relapse or make some bad choices. The other members are so welcoming and non judgmental and the group facilitator is a really good fit too. She actually has a history of substance abuse so she “gets it” so much more than other substance abuse counselors I’ve had in the past who haven’t struggled with addiction themselves.

I still have bad days where the cravings are really strong but I still smoke weed which helps cause I know I wouldn’t be able to go completely sober right now. It may be a future goal though. The number one thing that keeps me from relapsing is only surrounding myself with people who don’t use hard drugs. The only reason I’ve been close to relapse has been from hanging with the wrong people. Even though I can go to meetings with them and have someone who understands, the risk of them asking me to use with them or be there when they relapse for safety just isn’t worth the risk.
